correctness.rationale: Exact companion-matrix certificates M^22=I+N (mod 23), N^2=0, Nw=5(1,10,10^2), and M^506=I+23N (mod 529) are independently recomputed in the verifier. Since 10 has exact order 22, each branch slope 5*10^r is a unit modulo 23. An explicit matrix-binomial lifting lemma gives valuation 1+v23(h) for differences along 506-step subsequences and hence the exact branch isometry for every pair of nonnegative indices. Finite injection implies every branch permutes all residues modulo 23^k; the cyclic state basis has determinant -1 so the exact matrix order 22*23^k equals the scalar period. Exhaustive checks for k=1,2,3 and seeded modular tests corroborate, not replace, the infinite proof.

originality.rationale: The 2006 classification of p−1-periodic zero-free finite-field Padovan sequences is not the classical Padovan index sequence, which has period 506 modulo 23. The 2015 matrix-transform paper, the sequence database, and the later 2-adic shifted-valuation study do not state the 23-adic branch isometry or complete multiplicity law. The closest recovered private Perrin theorem applies to a different initial vector and gives a non-surjective spectrum; it cannot imply the Padovan equidistribution conclusion. Targeted mathematical-record and literature searches did not locate covering results. Absolute historical priority remains uncertain.
residual_risks: No historical search proves universal novelty; an unindexed paper may state a more general p-adic recurrence equidistribution criterion.
The 2024 related paper was inspected by accessible abstract rather than full body; published scope is at p=2.
The existing Perrin theorem has the same recurrence but a different initial vector; its underlying generic methods might simplify the present proof but do not establish its conclusion.

value.rationale: The ramified prime 23 of X^3−X−1 is a mathematically natural exceptional place to study local sequence images. The complete 23-adic isometry of all 22 index branches, the exact all-k distribution and least period are a structural classification of a classical integer recurrence. Unlike the related trace Perrin sequence, the Padovan initial vector gives 22 full-valued branches, showing a nontrivial dependence of local image geometry on the initial conditions. This is more than isolated congruences or finite tabulation.
